name: High-frequency wand
lead: A high-frequency wand is a handheld glass electrode that produces a low-current, high-voltage alternating current, giving a violet glow and ozone smell. It descends from the old Darsonval devices and is marketed for acne, pores and anti-aging.
It appears in skincare routines as a spot treatment, but the claims are largely unproven.

paras: The current is said to generate ozone and mild heat that kill acne bacteria and boost circulation. Only laboratory evidence supports an antibacterial effect.

Risks include irritation and burns from misuse, and it is contraindicated with pacemakers or pregnancy. The only study found tested a similar device in vitro against skin bacteria, with no human trials located, so the claims are unproven. It is not a substitute for proven acne treatment.
